_doc: Road events — the other half of js/encounters.js. In the user's words: 'Add more events like that too, to give the world more things to do as you wander around.' data/encounters.json already holds eleven set pieces, and every one of them is the same verb: bodies appear, you fight them. These are the ones that are NOT that. Each has a beat of its own — something to get out of a cage, something that runs and has to be caught, something that has to still be standing when the clock runs out, something that looks like treasure and is not, and something that is simply there for anyone who bothered to walk off the road. The engine for each `kind` is in js/encounters.js; this file only says which ones exist and how they are shaped. Original names and ideas only.

_schema.kind: which beat js/encounters.js runs: rescue | chase | defend | trap | find. Anything else is refused by tests/events.test.js, because an event nothing knows how to tick is an announcement and nothing more.
_schema.where: ring (out of sight) | ahead (down the line you are walking) | close (on top of you) — the same placement data/encounters.json uses.
_schema.count / escort / spread / prefer / aggro: the bodies, exactly as data/encounters.json shapes them. The set-piece builder is shared.
_schema.seconds: how long you have. A defend fails when it runs out; a chase gives up.
_schema.escapeAt: metres. A chase is lost if the runner gets this far from you.
_schema.springAt: metres. A trap springs when you come this close to the bait.
_schema.reward: { as: bag|chest, kind: a balance.json chest grade, name, gold: [lo,hi] } — a bag is dropped where the beat finished and is picked up by walking over it; a chest stands on the ground and is opened with E.
_schema.bait: a trap's or a find's chest: { kind, name } — placed the moment the event starts, because being able to see it from a distance is the whole hook.
_schema.win / fail / announce: the lines the player reads. Plain language, no exclamation marks.

events.name: Somebody in a cage
events.announce: There is a cage on a cart up ahead, and it is not empty.
events.win: The cage comes open. Whoever was in it does not wait to be thanked, but they leave you what the slavers had.
events.fail: You walk on. The cart goes the other way.
events.desc: Kill every guard and the captive is out. Nothing you can do to the cage itself — the guards have the key.

events.name: A pit with a lid on it
events.announce: Somebody is calling from under a grate, and somebody else is sitting on it.
events.win: The grate comes up. They were down there long enough to have gone through the pockets of everyone else who was.
events.fail: The calling stops before you reach it.
events.desc: A rescue with a champion sitting on the lid. The one that pays best of the two.

events.name: Something running with your money
events.announce: One of them breaks cover and runs, and it is carrying something.
events.win: You put it down. It was carrying more than it could spend.
events.fail: It gets over the rise and keeps going.
events.desc: Thirty-four seconds and a hundred and ninety metres. Movement speed and anything ranged is what wins this.

events.name: The one that got away
events.announce: Something wounded is going flat out across the open ground.
events.win: It goes down in the grass. Whatever it took from the last people through here is still on it.
events.desc: A named beast, already hurt, already running. The best-paid of the chases and the hardest to catch.

events.name: A cart with a wheel off
events.announce: A cart on its side, a strongbox still lashed to it, and somebody is coming for it.
events.win: The last of them goes down and the box is still shut. The carter is long gone; the box is not.
events.fail: They get the lashings off and take the box with them.
events.desc: The box is real and is standing there from the first second. Kill everything inside seventy-five seconds or it goes.

events.name: A watchfire nobody is standing at
events.announce: A fire still burning and the watch not at it. Something is working its way in.
events.win: It stays lit. Whoever was on watch left their locker behind, and you were the one who stayed.
events.fail: The fire goes out behind you.
events.desc: The night version, and harder. Ninety seconds against a bigger crowd, in the dark, for the same grade of box.

events.name: A chest in the open
events.announce: There is a chest sitting on its own in the middle of clear ground.
events.win: Whoever put it there is not going to need it.
events.desc: The chest is real and the loot is real. So is everything that comes out of the grass at eighteen metres.

events.name: An offering nobody collected
events.announce: Something has been left out on a flat stone, wrapped and tied.
events.win: The offering was always going to be paid for. It is still worth it.
events.desc: A warded chest, so it is worth springing on purpose. Bring something that hits more than one thing at a time.

events.name: A stone that has been moved
events.announce: One of these stones has been turned over, and not long ago.
events.win: Somebody hid this and did not come back for it.
events.desc: No fight at all. The whole event is that you went and looked at a thing that was slightly wrong.

events.name: A tree with something in it
events.announce: There is a split trunk a little off your line with something packed into it.
events.win: A courier's drop, or a thief's. Either way it is yours.
events.desc: The other no-fight one. These two are what make walking off the road ever worth doing.

events.name: Somebody's count
events.announce: Somebody has been keeping a tally on a rock out here, and it stops.
events.win: Whatever they were counting down to, they reached it. What they were saving is still here.
events.desc: The rare one of the three finds, and the best paid. Pure curiosity.
